newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Italy wins scant EU support for milk quota demand.
newsitem.headline: Italy wins scant EU support for milk quota demand.

text.p: Italy requested an increase in its European Union milk production quota to help match consumption but received little support at the Farm Council, EU officials said on Monday.
Italy is seeking a 600,000-tonne increase in its 9.9 million tonne annual EU milk quota to help fill a 40 percent consumption deficit according to Italian farmer estimates.
"An increase is urgently needed," Italian Farm Minister Michele Pinto told reporters.
But EU officials said that any further increase for Italy could trigger similar demands from other EU member states.
Pinto said that Spain, Greece and Britain, which are all facing fines for exceeding 1995/96 EU milk quotas, intervened during a debate to say that the Italian case was well-founded.
Pinto added that the Italian government was not calling into question EU fines totalling 170-million-Ecus but wanted the problem of Italian quotas to be discussed in a broader context.
Dutch Farm Minister Jozias Van Aartsen told a news conference that Italian quotas would be examined as part of a milk market analysis being prepared by the EU's executive European Commission.
EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler, who will hold private talks with Pinto on Tuesday, said the problem should be tackled on a step by step basis.
Fischler noted that a 900,000-tonne increase in the Italian milk quota was agreed in the early 1990s despite its late implementation of EU quotas introduced in 1984.

Italian farmers, demonstrating against EU milk quotas, lifted a four-day blockade of roads leading to Milan's main airport on Monday after Prime Minister Romano Prodi promised to hear their grievances.
Prodi told reporters on Saturday that the government would give financial aid to the farmers in the form of soft loans but could not pay their fines.
